record.what_it_does: Customer messaging, support inbox and helpdesk platform with Fin AI agent.
record.auth_notes: There are two ways to authenticate, and both are sent as Authorization: Bearer. An Access Token works for private apps and scripts against your own workspace. OAuth is for apps that access other people's Intercom data. The docs say apps must use OAuth rather than asking users for Access Tokens, and that asking for tokens breaks Intercom's terms of service.
record.access_notes: Anyone can create a developer workspace without being an Intercom customer, and the FAQ says these workspaces are free. That gives a developer an Access Token and a dev OAuth app with no gate. Dev workspaces have limits: no email sending, no push notifications, articles can't go live, at most 20 users/leads, and they can't be converted to production. No expiry is documented. Distributing an OAuth app to other workspaces needs Intercom review, whether the app is listed or unlisted, and review takes up to 7 business days. Until approved, the app can only be used by your own team. Some endpoints can return 403 "API Plan restricted" depending on the customer's plan.
record.api_breadth_notes: The REST API covers contacts, companies, conversations, tickets, articles/help center, data events, tags, notes, teams, admins, segments, messages, data connectors and more. Operations weren't counted exactly but are well over 50. Intercom publishes an official OpenAPI description at github.com/intercom/intercom-openapi.
record.mcp_notes: US: https://mcp.intercom.com/mcp. EU: https://mcp.eu.intercom.com/mcp. Each region also has a deprecated SSE endpoint at /sse. AU workspaces aren't supported yet. Auth is OAuth (recommended) or a bearer token. The Fin Operator tools need an OAuth connection and a workspace that has Fin Operator.
record.blocker_notes: Development and testing are fully self-serve through a free developer workspace. A public OAuth app that installs into end users' workspaces must pass Intercom's review first, whether listed or unlisted, and review can take up to 7 business days. Any later changes need re-approval. Until then the app works only for the developer's own team.

evidence.quote: apps are required to use OAuth rather than asking users for Access Tokens
An Access Token is for if you're using the API to access data in your own Intercom workspace.
Developer workspaces are free and intended for development purposes only.
You do not have to be an existing Intercom customer in order to create a dev workspace.
Both unlisted and listed apps must be submitted for review.
During this process, your app will be private and can only be used by you and your team.
The Intercom MCP server is available for US and EU hosted workspaces. AU hosted workspaces are not yet supported.
Webhooks are a way that you can access real-time notifications about events that happen in your Intercom workspace.
This repository contains OpenAPI descriptions for Intercom's REST API.
